transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um, I guess I came in because my mind is just... it's constantly jumping all over the place. Like, I can't stop it. It jumps from worrying if our lab's new partnership is going to end up cutting my position... which, honestly, the guys from the new partner company are so clueless. They came in last Tuesday for a tour, wearing these ridiculous expensive suits, and one of them almost knocked over a tray of polymer samples I'd been prepping all morning. Didn't even apologize, just looked at me like I was the one in the way. It's like, do you even know what a controlled environment is? 

But anyway, I just keep thinking they're going to fire me, or... or that my data is all wrong. And if my data is wrong, I feel like I've already ruined my chances at grad school. I was looking at this materials science program in the Midwest, actually. My cousin lives out there and he says the housing market is super cheap right now, he just bought a place with a huge backyard for his golden retriever, which is great because those dogs really need space to run or they get destructive... 

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, so grad school feels ruined, and then I start stressing that my bills are going to pile up, and I just know my family thinks I'm completely falling behind everyone else my age... it's just everything, all at once, all day.
Do you find that you worry excessively about a number of different things in your life, even when there isn't a clear reason to be concerned?

Yeah, exactly. It's just... it's like a motor that won't shut off. I mean, I know I just said it, but I'm constantly worrying about everything. Like, the lab partnership cutting my job, which is a very real possibility because corporate mergers always lead to "redundancies," right? That's what they call it. My uncle went through that in the 90s when he worked in manufacturing. He ended up having to sell his boat, which was a shame because we used to go fishing on it every summer. He had this little cabin up by the lake... 

But yeah, I worry about the job, and then my brain just spirals into, well, what if my data is wrong? And if the data is wrong, I'm never getting into grad school. And then I start thinking about my bills piling up, and how my family probably looks at me and thinks I'm just this massive failure who's falling behind everyone else. It's just... it's exhausting, honestly. I don't even need a reason, my brain just finds things to panic about.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling tense, or being easily fatigued, that seem to go along with all this worrying?

Yeah, I definitely get tense. Like, at work, I feel so wound up that I can't even settle into my chair. I'm constantly tapping my foot, checking my messages, or just walking back to the instrument room for literally no reason. And honestly, the instrument room is always freezing because they keep the AC cranked up to protect the mass specs. I told the facilities guy—Dave, I think his name is—that we need a better thermostat in there, but he just mumbled something about budget cuts and walked away. Dave's always complaining about budget cuts. He drives this massive truck that probably costs a fortune in gas, so I don't know why he's so worried about the building's budget. 

But anyway, yeah, I'm just restless all the time. And I get startled by the most normal lab noises, like someone dropping a beaker or the centrifuge beeping. It just makes me jump out of my skin.
Have you noticed yourself feeling fatigued or low on energy a lot of the time, even if you haven’t been physically active?

Yeah, I'm just... I'm always exhausted. It's like, even if I actually manage to stay in bed for a full night, I wake up feeling like I just pulled an all-nighter cramming for organic chem. Which I used to do a lot in undergrad, actually. My roommate, Greg, he'd stay up with me, but he was a business major, so he wasn't even studying half the time, just playing video games on his laptop. He had one of those glowing keyboards that changed colors, which was super distracting when I was trying to memorize reaction mechanisms. I think he works in real estate now or something. 

But um, yeah, the tiredness. By the time I'm at work, just doing simple stuff like labeling samples, or even later when I'm at home trying to cook dinner for my family... my body just feels so heavy. Like, physically heavy. And my brain is just totally drained. I don't even have the energy to chop vegetables most nights, which sucks because my mom bought me this really nice chef's knife for my birthday... but yeah, I just have zero energy, all the time.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once liked?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I still like doing the things I usually do. Like playing guitar, I still try to play when I can. My dad actually taught me how to play when I was like, twelve. He had this old acoustic Fender that he bought at a pawn shop in the 80s, and it had this huge scratch down the back from where he dropped it on a camping trip. We used to go camping a lot up in the Adirondacks, usually in late August when the bugs weren't as bad. My mom hated it because she always ended up getting mosquito bites all over her ankles, no matter how much bug spray she used. She swore by that natural citronella stuff, but I always told her the chemical DEET is the only thing that actually works. I mean, I'm a chemist, I know how these compounds interact with olfactory receptors... 

But yeah, anyway, I still enjoy playing guitar and stuff. I just don't always have the energy for it because I'm so tired all the time, like I said. But the interest is definitely still there.
Do you find it hard to concentrate on tasks, even ones you're familiar with, because your mind keeps wandering or getting distracted?

Yeah, actually. It's really hard to focus lately. Like, I'll be right in the middle of a titration, something I've done a thousand times, and suddenly my mind is just... gone. I'm thinking about whether I left the stove on, or if I paid the electric bill. Which reminds me, the electric company just switched to this new online portal thing, and it is so poorly designed. The user interface is a complete mess. It took me like twenty minutes just to figure out how to update my credit card info because my old card expired. And the new card they sent me has this weird vertical layout instead of the normal horizontal one. I don't know why banks are doing that now, it makes it so awkward to put into the chip reader at the grocery store. The cashier at Trader Joe's was looking at me like I was an idiot because I kept trying to insert it the wrong way. She had this really bright purple hair, like, neon purple. It actually looked pretty cool, I wonder what brand of dye she uses... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, concentrating. Yeah, I just... I can't keep my train of thought on what I'm supposed to be doing. My brain just spins off into a million different directions, even when I'm trying really hard to just focus on my work.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up earlier than planned, even when you're tired?

No, not really. I usually pass out pretty fast once I'm in bed. I actually just got this new mattress topper, it's this polyurethane foam blend that's supposedly infused with copper for thermal regulation. Which is mostly just marketing nonsense, honestly, because the thermal conductivity of copper particles suspended in a polymer matrix like that isn't going to significantly alter the macroscopic heat transfer of the bed. I tried explaining the thermodynamics of it to the guy at the mattress store, but he just kept pointing at his little brochure. He was wearing this really overpowering cologne, too, smelled exactly like this synthetic musk we used to synthesize in organic lab sophomore year. It gave me a massive headache. We actually had to evacuate the lab once because some kid named Brian accidentally heated his flask too fast and it shattered everywhere. Brian was always breaking glassware, the professor hated him... 

But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, sleep. Yeah, no, falling asleep and staying asleep is fine. I don't wake up early or anything like that. I just sleep the whole night and still wake up feeling completely dead, like I said before.
Do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most of the time, even when there isn't a specific reason for it?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down like that. I mean, I worry a lot, obviously, but it's not like a sadness thing. It's more of a... a constant buzzing in my head. Speaking of buzzing, the fluorescent lights in my lab have been making this awful humming noise for three days straight. It's a 60-hertz hum, probably a failing magnetic ballast in the fixture. I put in a maintenance request, but the facilities guy, Gary, is always dragging his feet. Gary is the same guy who took two weeks to fix the fume hood last month. He was telling me all about his son's baseball tournament while he was supposed to be working on it. They went all the way to Ohio for this tournament, and apparently they stayed in this motel that had a pool shaped like a guitar. Which is kind of funny because I was just talking about my dad's guitar earlier. But anyway, Gary's son plays shortstop, and... 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, feeling down. No, no, I don't really feel depressed most of the time. Just really, really wound up.
